is_anopheles.evidence: The study focuses on Anopheles stephensi (page 1, Abstract).

reports_target_markers.evidence: The study reports genotyping for Vgsc L995F/S (kdr L1014F/S) and Ace-1 G280S (ace-1R G119S) (page 4, Results).

reports_extractable_genotype_data.evidence: The paper states: 'Of the 51 An. stephensi examined for kdr mutations, none carried the L1014 mutation. In addition, 30 An. stephensi were analysed for ace1 mutations... Overall, none of the An. stephensi genotyped carried the ace1R G119S mutation.' (page 4, Results).

african_field_population.evidence: Mosquitoes were collected from Kebri Dehar, Ethiopia (page 2, Methods).

is_primary_study.evidence: This is an empirical study reporting new field data (page 1, Abstract).

sub_country_location.evidence: Samples were collected in Kebri Dehar, Somali Regional State, Ethiopia (page 2, Methods).

temporal_resolution_within_3y.evidence: Collections took place from November to December 2016 (page 2, Methods).

duplicate_risk.evidence: The study describes a new collection of An. stephensi in Kebri Dehar in 2016.

supplement.evidence: All necessary data is provided in the main text and tables.

assessment.summary: This study evaluated insecticide resistance in Anopheles stephensi collected from Kebri Dehar, Ethiopia, in 2016. Bioassays showed resistance to multiple insecticide classes. Molecular analysis of 51 specimens for kdr (L1014F/S) and 30 specimens for ace-1 (G119S) revealed no resistance-associated mutations.
